How often should you clean a water tank in Gurugram?

The short answer is every 6 months: once before summer and once after the monsoon. Here is why that rhythm suits Gurugram, and when your tank may need attention sooner.

The 6-month rule, and why it fits Gurugram

Most homes in Gurugram store water twice: an underground concrete sump that receives municipal or tanker supply, and a plastic tank on the roof that feeds the taps. Both slowly collect fine silt that settles on the floor as a soft layer of mud. Leave it long enough and it starts to lift every time the tank refills, which is when you notice cloudy water in a bucket or grit in a tap filter.

Cleaning every 6 months keeps that layer thin. It also lines up neatly with the two seasons that are hardest on stored water here:

  • Before summer (March to April): rooftop tanks sit in direct sun through May and June. Warm water and light let algae spread over the walls and under the lid. Starting the season with a clean tank makes a big difference.
  • After the monsoon (September to October): supply water is often muddier during the rains, so the sump and the rooftop tank both pick up a thicker layer of sludge.

If you only remember one thing, book a cleaning around Holi and again around Diwali.

When to clean sooner than 6 months

Some homes need a shorter gap. Consider cleaning every 3 to 4 months if any of these apply to you:

  • You rely heavily on tanker water, which can vary a lot in quality from load to load.
  • Your tank lid is cracked, loose or missing, so dust, leaves, insects or birds can get in.
  • The underground sump has a manhole cover that does not seal well, or you have seen seepage near it.
  • Someone at home has a weak immune system, or you have a small baby, and you want to be extra careful.
  • You have recently had construction or renovation work nearby, which puts a lot of dust in the air.

Also clean straight away if you notice a smell, a change in colour, slime on the walls or a sudden drop in pressure. Our guide on signs your water tank needs cleaning goes through these in detail.

Clean the sump and rooftop tank together

A common mistake is cleaning only the rooftop tank because it is easy to reach. The sump is upstream: whatever sludge sits in it is pumped up to the roof the next time the motor runs. Within a few weeks the rooftop tank can look as if it was never cleaned. Doing both on the same visit is the simplest way to get a result that lasts. You can read more about how we handle sumps on the underground tank cleaning page.

Does an RO or filter mean I can skip cleaning?

No. An RO or a tap filter treats the water at one point, usually the kitchen. The bathrooms, the washing machine and the shower all draw straight from the rooftop tank. A clean tank also means the RO pre-filters and sediment cartridges clog less often.

Planning cleaning for a society or several tanks

For apartment societies and RWAs, the 6-month cycle is easiest to manage as a fixed schedule: one round in spring and one after the rains, with residents told in advance when water will be off. Societies with 5 or more tanks get bulk rates. See the society tank cleaning page for how a multi-tank visit is planned.

Each tank usually takes about 60 to 90 minutes, so a home with one sump and one rooftop tank is normally done in a single morning.

Questions

How often should a rooftop water tank be cleaned in Gurugram?

Every 6 months is a good routine: once before summer and once after the monsoon. Clean sooner if you see algae, smell anything unusual or the lid is damaged.

How often should an underground sump be cleaned?

Also about every 6 months, ideally on the same visit as the rooftop tank, because sludge from the sump is pumped up to the roof.

What is the best month to clean a water tank in Gurugram?

March to April before the summer heat, and September to October after the monsoon, are the most useful times.
